data.title: Ketoconazole + Clobetasone butyrate cream
data.summary: V Steroid combinations · Combination: imidazole antifungal (ketoconazole 2%) + moderate-potency steroid (clobetasone butyrate 0.05%, UK 'moderate')
data.body:
_Topicals · V Steroid combinations_

**Class:** Combination: imidazole antifungal (ketoconazole 2%) + moderate-potency steroid (clobetasone butyrate 0.05%, UK 'moderate')

## Mechanism of action
- Ketoconazole: anti-Malassezia, anti-dermatophyte, mild anti-inflammatory
- Clobetasone butyrate: moderate steroid (much weaker than clobetasol — do not confuse the names)

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Short-term for inflamed seborrhoeic dermatitis (face, flexures) and inflamed intertrigo
- Not recommended for tinea

## Dose & formulations
- Once or twice daily for up to 1–2 weeks, then plain ketoconazole for maintenance

## Adverse effects
- Steroid side effects with prolonged use: perioral dermatitis, rosacea, atrophy; tinea incognito

## Contraindications
- Tinea, rosacea, acne, perioral dermatitis; long-term use on face

## Pregnancy & lactation
Avoid prolonged use.

## Viva points
- Clobetasone (moderate) ≠ clobetasol (super-potent) — classic confusion
- Rationale is seborrhoeic dermatitis, not tinea

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.45; Khopkar ch.22. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
